source: A low and a high for each row a household commonly leaves blank, wide enough to hold most US households: spending lines from the BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2023 tables (food at home plus away, shelter, transportation) read as roughly the 10th and 90th percentile of household spending; balances from the Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances 2022 (transaction accounts, retirement accounts) at the 25th and 90th percentile for households under 55; pay from the Census Current Population Survey 2024 (household income, 20th to 90th percentile); card rates from the Federal Reserve G.19 release 2025 (assessed interest 20% to 30%) with a floor for promotional rates.
confidenceNote: The bounds are typed from memory of those tables, not copied from them; verify against the published releases before they are presented as figures. They are used only to size a swing (the insight at the low end against the high end), never as a value, so a bound being off by a fifth changes the size of a caution, not a number in any room.
note: Keyed by row id (data/ledger-rows.json). low and high in the row's unit (cents for money, a fraction for a rate). feeds names the insight the swing is measured on: fiMonths (months to FI), runwayMonths, netWorthCents, takeHomeMonthlyCents, reachableCents, interestMonthlyCents. engines/notknowing.js sets the row to each bound on a copy of the household and reads the insight at both. I2, D-214.
